One-call E2SFCA accessibility map

Source: R/accessibility_map.R
mysterymaps_accessibility_map.Rd

Joins a twostep::compute_e2sfca() result onto its tract geometry and renders it with the three-way zero/outside/missing distinction the result already carries – in one call, instead of each caller re-deriving the join and the colour classification by hand.

Usage

mysterymaps_accessibility_map(
  e2sfca_result,
  tracts_sf,
  value_col = "access_scaled",
  legend_title = "Modeled Accessibility",
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  k = 6,
  digits = 1,
  zero_color = "#e0e0e0",
  na_color = "#ffffff",
  outside_color = "#efe7d5",
  viridis_option = "viridis",
  crs = 5070
)

Arguments

e2sfca_result

list: the object twostep::compute_e2sfca() returns. Must contain an access element: a data frame with columns GEOID, coverage_status, and value_col.

tracts_sf

sf polygon layer with a GEOID column to join e2sfca_result$access onto.

value_col

character(1): column in e2sfca_result$access to map. Default "access_scaled" – the per-capita-scaled score (e.g. "per 100,000 women"), which compute_e2sfca()'s own documentation names as the scientific value a reader, table or map should consume. Pass "access" for the unscaled score.

legend_title

character(1): legend heading. Default "Modeled Accessibility".

title, subtitle, caption

Character labels. NULL omits.

k

integer(1): target number of Jenks classes for the positive scores, passed to mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale(). Default 6.

digits

integer(1): decimal places in the legend's score labels. Default 1.

zero_color, na_color, outside_color

Colours for a measured zero, a missing value, and a tract outside every modelled catchment, respectively. Defaults match mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale()'s own.

viridis_option

character(1): passed to the option argument of the viridisLite::viridis() palette used for the positive classes.

crs

Projection for display. Default EPSG:5070 (Albers Equal Area), appropriate for the contiguous United States.

Value

A ggplot object. The caller saves it; this function writes nothing.

Details

compute_e2sfca()'s $access tibble distinguishes three states that a plain continuous choropleth collapses into two:

a measured zero

coverage_status == "within_modeled_catchment" and the accessibility score is 0 – the tract is reached, and the weighted supply reaching it is genuinely nil. Takes zero_color.

outside every catchment

coverage_status == "outside_all_modeled_catchments" – no isochrone reaches this tract at all. This is the finding an access study usually exists to report, and is emphatically not missing data. Takes outside_color.

missing

value_col is NA for a reached tract, or the tract's GEOID has no match in tracts_sf. Takes na_color.

Before this distinction existed in twostep, outside-catchment tracts were zero-filled and became indistinguishable from a measured zero – 190 of 1,447 Colorado tracts, 13% of the state, each reported as "zero accessibility" when the honest answer was "the model never reached here". mysterymaps_jenks_zero_scale()'s coverage argument exists specifically for this shape, via coverage_status; this function is the one-call assembler for it, the same role mysterymaps_county_access_map() plays for a plain leaflet supply choropleth.

This function does not call twostep::compute_e2sfca() itself and does not depend on the twostep package – it only consumes the list shape that function documents returning, so a caller can pass in anything with the same shape.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# The shape compute_e2sfca() returns -- see twostep::compute_e2sfca()'s own
# examples for how `access` is actually produced from provider isochrones.
e2sfca_result <- list(access = data.frame(
  GEOID = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"),
  access_scaled = c(0, 4.2, NA, 7.8),
  coverage_status = c("within_modeled_catchment", "within_modeled_catchment",
                      "outside_all_modeled_catchments", "within_modeled_catchment")
))
tracts_sf <- sf::st_sf(
  GEOID = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T4"),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(lapply(1:4, function(i) {
    x <- -100 + i
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(x, x + 1, x + 1, x, x), c(40, 40, 41, 41, 40))))
  }), crs = 4326)
)
mysterymaps_accessibility_map(e2sfca_result, tracts_sf)
}
